{"id":"PKIX-q9hv.29","title":"Error::ProfileViolation / ::OcspDelegation stringly-typed reason field is non-idiomatic for a public error","description":"Two Error variants carry only a fixed-string 'reason' as their payload (lib.rs:173-199):

    Error::ProfileViolation { reason: Cow<'static, str> }
    Error::OcspDelegation   { reason: Cow<'static, str> }

The rustdoc on each field documents the design (lines 170-181, 190-198): the reason is a 'fixed-string description suitable for logging' and explicitly tells callers 'pattern-match on the variant rather than the inner string'. That documentation is honest about the constraint, but the constraint itself is the smell: programmatic callers get one bit of discriminator (which variant) for what is internally a many-way classification.

Today the producers in this PR write five distinct ProfileViolation reason strings:
  - 'TSA certificate has no ExtendedKeyUsage extension' (two arms, lib.rs:1427, 1433 — already flagged by PKIX-q9hv.15 area)
  - 'TSA ExtendedKeyUsage extension must be marked critical (RFC 3161 §2.3)'
  - 'TSA ExtendedKeyUsage extension is malformed'
  - 'TSA ExtendedKeyUsage must contain only id-kp-timeStamping (RFC 3161 §2.3)'
  - 'TSA KeyUsage extension is malformed'
  - 'TSA KeyUsage must contain only digitalSignature and/or nonRepudiation (...)'

A caller that wants to log 'TSA EKU not critical' counts vs. 'TSA EKU not sole' counts cannot do so without grepping the reason text — a notoriously fragile pattern across release boundaries.

Idiomatic Rust answer: replace the string field with a sub-enum.

    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    #[non_exhaustive]
    pub enum ProfileViolationKind {
        TsaEkuExtensionMissing,
        TsaEkuNotCritical,
        TsaEkuMalformed,
        TsaEkuNotSoleTimestamping,
        TsaKeyUsageMalformed,
        TsaKeyUsageForbiddenBit, // could carry the offending bit
        // ... add more as wrappers grow
    }
    ProfileViolation(ProfileViolationKind)

Display can still produce the same fixed-string output via match. Callers gain programmatic dispatch; the workspace gains a place to attach structured data later (e.g. 'TsaKeyUsageForbiddenBit { bit: KeyUsageBit }') without churning the outer Error API. AGENTS.md §error-handling explicitly flags this anti-pattern: 'Error variants that wrap String for the message instead of structured fields. Err(format!("expected {x}, got {y}")) loses the values; a structured variant keeps them accessible to callers who want to handle them.'

Adjacent but distinct from PKIX-q9hv.19 (non_exhaustive on the struct-variant shape). That fix freezes the variant shape; this fix changes the shape from string-typed to enum-typed. Both apply.

Cost of leaving it: forever-commitment to stringly-typed sub-classification. Pre-1.0 is the cheap time to fix. Post-1.0 the sub-enum becomes a breaking change.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-05-14T14:56:56Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-05-14T14:56:56Z","metadata":{},"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"","depends_on_id":"PKIX-q9hv","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-05-14T07:56:55Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"Analysis 2026-11-25: pair this with PKIX-q9hv.19 and land them together.

q9hv.19 wants #[non_exhaustive] on the ProfileViolation / OcspDelegation struct variants. Adding it alone is a poor trade: it forbids construction outside pkix-chain (breaking pkix-chain/tests/serde_round_trip.rs, which builds both variants), and it protects only against ADDED fields -- whereas replacing  with a typed classification, which is what this bead asks for, changes the field's type and breaks destructuring callers regardless.

So the sequence is: settle the payload type here, then add #[non_exhaustive] and decide construction (a constructor fn, or relocate the serde cases in-crate) in the same breaking change. See q9hv.19's notes for the detail.

Current consumers for reference: pkix-tlsrpt/src/classify.rs matches with { .. } and survives either change; pkix-chain's own integration tests destructure { reason } and will need updating whichever way this goes."}

{"notes":"Analysis 2026-11-25: pair this with PKIX-q9hv.19 and land them together.

q9hv.19 wants #[non_exhaustive] on the ProfileViolation / OcspDelegation struct variants. Adding it alone is a poor trade: it forbids construction outside pkix-chain (breaking pkix-chain/tests/serde_round_trip.rs, which builds both variants directly), and it protects only against ADDED fields -- whereas replacing the reason field with a typed classification, which is what this bead asks for, changes the field TYPE and breaks destructuring callers regardless.

So the sequence is: settle the payload type here, then add #[non_exhaustive] and decide construction (a constructor fn, or relocate the serde cases in-crate) in the same breaking change. See q9hv.19 notes for the detail.

Current consumers for reference: pkix-tlsrpt/src/classify.rs matches with { .. } and survives either change; pkix-chain own integration tests destructure { reason } and will need updating whichever way this goes."}

Fixed together, per your ruling, which is how the pair had to land.

q9hv.29 asked for a typed classification instead of the fixed string; q9hv.19 asked for #[non_exhaustive] on the two struct variants. My earlier analysis said doing q9hv.19 alone was a poor trade, because it costs external construction while protecting only against ADDED FIELDS -- and retyping the payload, which is what q9hv.29 wants, breaks destructuring callers regardless. Doing both in one change pays the cost once.

ProfileViolationKind: six variants, every one an RFC 3161 time-stamping rule, because that is the only profile with post-validation checks in this crate. OcspDelegationKind: four. Both enums #[non_exhaustive], so further kinds are additive. Display on each reproduces the exact message the old string carried, so log output is unchanged.

Both VARIANTS are #[non_exhaustive] as q9hv.19 asked. That blocks struct-literal construction outside the crate, which is the cost I flagged -- pkix-chain/tests/serde_round_trip.rs constructs both. Resolved with Error::profile_violation(kind) and Error::ocsp_delegation(kind), which tests, mocks and adapters need and which read better than a struct literal anyway.

The payoff is visible in the five tests that had to change, all of which were sniffing the string: reason.contains("critical"), contains("only id-kp-timeStamping"), contains("KeyUsage"), contains("issuer DN"), contains("signature"). All five are now assert_eq! against a named kind. The best illustration is the last: its comment read "the reason must point at the signature-binding failure, not the DN gate -- both surface as OcspDelegation but mean different things diagnostically". That is precisely the distinction the typed payload makes first-class rather than inferred from prose, and it is the DN-twin attack the binding exists to catch.

Serde: the old test turned on Cow content-based equality surviving Borrowed-to-Owned. It now round-trips every kind and additionally asserts no two kinds share a wire form -- otherwise caching an error and reloading it would silently lose the classification, which is the use case serde on these types is for.

Unaffected consumers: pkix-tlsrpt/src/classify.rs and both pkix-difftest oracles match with { .. }, so they needed no change -- which is the #[non_exhaustive] discipline working as intended.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos, 2357 tests, workspace feature powerset 241 combinations clean.
